title: Managed DNS provider under DDoS makes the company's domains unresolvable
source_note: Failure pattern follows the 2016 Dyn cyberattack: a DDoS against a managed DNS provider made many customers' domains unresolvable, an outage entirely outside the affected companies' own infrastructure. All services, provider names, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~12:00 UTC many users cannot reach the site at all, and some outbound API calls are failing intermittently. Our servers look healthy. Reports say a DNS provider is having problems.

signal_lines.msg: external DNS resolution success for www.example.com down to 60% from multiple regions
DNS provider dyn-managed reports a large DDoS against its infrastructure since 11:58 UTC
intermittent resolution failures for third-party endpoints (payments, email); ~20% of individual outbound calls fail to resolve, so a multi-call checkout succeeds only ~65% of the time
origin servers and internal DNS are healthy; failures are all at the external authoritative layer
secondary DNS provider activated for critical zones; resolution success climbing back toward 99%

ground_truth.root_cause: The managed DNS provider hosting the company's public DNS zones was hit by a large DDoS starting ~11:58 UTC (confirmed by the provider). External resolution of the company's own domains - and of some third-party endpoints on the same provider - became unreliable, dropping to ~55% success from multiple regions, so users could not reliably reach the site and ~20% of outbound third-party calls failed at DNS resolution. Internal DNS and the origin servers were healthy; the failure was entirely at the external authoritative DNS layer, which the company does not operate. The mitigation was to activate a secondary DNS provider for critical zones.
evidence_path: edge-monitor: external DNS resolution success for the company's domain drops to ~60% from multiple regions
the DNS provider reports a large DDoS against its infrastructure since 11:58 UTC
api-gateway sees intermittent resolution failures for third-party endpoints; ~20% of outbound calls fail to resolve
origin servers and internal DNS are confirmed healthy - failures are all at the external authoritative layer
resolution recovers after a secondary DNS provider is activated for critical zones
ground_truth.fix: Activate a secondary DNS provider for critical zones (done). Run authoritative DNS across two independent providers permanently, and cache last-known-good resolutions for critical third-party endpoints.
